content: 1. The dosage forms of dolutegravir (e.g., Tivicay and Tivicay PD) are not bioequivalent and cannot be used interchangeably. 2. Poor virologic response has been observed in patients treated with dolutegravir 50 mg twice daily when they have an INSTI-resistance Q148 substitution along with two or more additional INSTI-resistance substitutions, such as L74I/M, E138A/D/K/T, G140A/S, Y143H/R, E157Q, G163E/K/Q/R/S, or G193E/R. 3. In patients with underlying hepatitis B or C, hepatic enzyme levels should be measured prior to initiating dolutegravir therapy and monitored periodically thereafter. 4. Pregnancy testing should be performed before starting dolutegravir in females of childbearing potential. 5. Dolutegravir is indicated in combination with other antiretroviral therapies (ARTs) for treatment-naïve or treatment-experienced but INSTI-naïve children aged ≥4 weeks and weighing ≥3 kg. 6. When co-administering dolutegravir with potent UGT1A or CYP3A inducers (e.g., efavirenz, fosamprenavir/ritonavir, tipranavir/ritonavir, rifampin), the weight-based dose of dolutegravir should be increased to twice daily. 7. Dolutegravir increases the plasma concentration of dofetilide by inhibiting renal clearance, which can lead to life-threatening arrhythmias. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Aluminum hydroxide or magnesium carbonate decreases dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after such medications. 9. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued at least 1 month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for elimination of the medications. 10. Carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 11. Efavirenz decreases dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. The dolutegravir dose should be increased to 50 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong UGT1A/CYP3A inducers. 12. Etravirine significantly reduces dolutegravir plasma concentrations. However, this effect is mitigated by co-administration with lopinavir/ritonavir, darunavir/ritonavir, or atazanavir/ritonavir. Etravirine should not be used without these agents. 13. Magnesium-containing medications (e.g., magnesium citrate, magnesium oxide, magnesium hydroxide) decrease dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after such medications. 14. Rifampin decreases dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. The dolutegravir dose should be increased when co-administered with strong UGT1A/CYP3A inducers. 15. Zinc-containing medications decrease dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Dolutegravir should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after oral zinc salts. 16. Orlistat may decrease dolutegravir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. HIV RNA levels should be monitored frequently, and orlistat should be discontinued if an increase in viral load is confirmed. 17. Selenium decreases dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Dolutegravir should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after selenium-containing medications. 18. Multivitamins containing polyvalent cations decrease dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after such multivitamins. 19. Calcium-containing medications (e.g., calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium citrate) decrease dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after such medications. 20. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate decreases dolutegravir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Dolutegravir should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after such medications. 21. Ublituximab may decrease the effects of dolutegravir due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be closely monitored. 22. Metformin levels may be increased by dolutegravir due to inhibition of renal organic cation transporter 2 (OCT2). The total daily dose of metformin should be limited to 1,000 mg when used with dolutegravir, and blood glucose levels should be monitored. 23. Ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate decrease dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after such medications. 24. St. John’s Wort decreases dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. 25. Sucralfate decreases dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after sucralfate. 26. Phenobarbital, phenytoin, and oxcarbazepine decrease dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided due to insufficient data to recommend dosage adjustments. 27. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of betibeglogene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 28. Dolutegravir increases the levels of dalfampridine by inhibiting OCT2 and multidrug and toxin extrusion transporter 1 (MATE1). Therapy should be closely monitored. 29. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve inhibition of systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. 30. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases dolutegravir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Dolutegravir should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium.
